args.query: What is the learnable class token in ViT and how is its final state used for classification?
In DeiT's distillation-token procedure, which target (hard label or teacher prediction) trains the class branch and which trains the distillation branch?
How does DeiT's described late-fusion inference combine the class-branch and distillation-branch outputs?

args.instructions: Answer the question directly in the first sentence. Then compare what each paper says, naming the paper for every point, and state where the papers agree, disagree or report numbers that are not comparable. If one hop of the question is not answered by the evidence, say which.

result.answer: ViT's [class] token is an extra learnable embedding prepended to the patch embeddings; its state at the Transformer encoder output is the image representation, which a classification head turns into the class prediction [S:2ec4ef3fa836#19]. In DeiT's distillation-token procedure, the class branch is trained with the true/ground-truth class label, while the distillation branch is trained with the teacher's hard predicted label [S:4cebd2b97b41#28]. At inference, DeiT's late fusion adds the softmax outputs of the separate linear classifiers on the class and distillation embeddings to make the prediction [S:4cebd2b97b41#33].

claims.text: ViT prepends a learnable [class] embedding to the patch embeddings, and that token's final encoder state serves as the image representation.
claims.note: Span states a learnable embedding is prepended and its encoder output serves as the image representation.

claims.text: ViT's classification head is implemented by an MLP with one hidden layer at pre-training time and by a single linear layer at fine-tuning time.
claims.note: Span exactly describes MLP with one hidden layer at pre-training and a single linear layer at fine-tuning.

claims.text: DeiT's class token is a trainable vector appended before the first layer that passes through the transformer layers and is linearly projected to predict the class.
claims.note: Span states the class token is trainable, appended before the first layer, passes through transformer layers, and is linearly projected.

claims.text: DeiT's distillation token is trained to reproduce the teacher's hard predicted label instead of the true label.
claims.note: Span says the distillation token reproduces the teacher's hard predicted label instead of the true label.

claims.text: Both the class and distillation tokens input to DeiT's transformers are learned by back-propagation.
claims.note: Span explicitly states both class and distillation tokens are learned by back-propagation.

claims.text: DeiT's late fusion attaches separate linear classifiers to the class and distillation embeddings and adds their softmax outputs to make the prediction.
claims.note: Span describes separate linear classifiers for class and distillation embeddings and late fusion by adding softmax outputs.

claims.text: DeiT's architecture is identical to ViT's with no convolutions, differing only in training strategies and the distillation token, and it uses a linear classifier rather than an MLP head for pre-training.
claims.note: Span says the architecture is identical with no convolutions, differs in training strategies and distillation token, and uses a linear classifier rather than an MLP head for pre-training.

citations.title: arXiv:2012.12877v2  [cs.CV]  15 Jan 2021
citations.text:
The class token
is a trainable vector, appended to the patch tokens before the
ﬁrst layer, that goes through the transformer layers, and is then projected with
a linear layer to predict the class. This class token is inherited from NLP [14],
and departs from the typical pooling layers used in computer vision to predict
the class. The transformer thus process batches of (N + 1) tokens of dimension
D, of which only the class vector is used to predict the output. This architecture
forces the self-attention to spread information between the patch tokens and
the class token: at training time the supervision signal comes only from the
class embedding, while the patch tokens are the model’s only variable input.

Figure 2: Our distillation procedure: we simply include a new distillation token.
It interacts with the class and patch tokens through the self-attention layers.
This distillation token is employed in a similar fashion as the class token, ex-
cept that on output of the network its objective is to reproduce the (hard) label
predicted by the teacher, instead of true label. Both the class and distillation
tokens input to the transformers are learned by back-propagation.

citations.title: arXiv:2012.12877v2  [cs.CV]  15 Jan 2021
citations.text:
Classiﬁcation with our approach: joint classiﬁers.
At test time, both the
class or the distillation embeddings produced by the transformer are associ-
ated with linear classiﬁers and able to infer the image label. Yet our referent
method is the late fusion of these two separate heads, for which we add the
softmax output by the two classiﬁers to make the prediction. We evaluate these
three options in Section 5.
